2610.05413.title: A Strong Baseline for Evaluating Vision Encoders in Multimodal Large Language Models
2610.05413.paper_summary: Evaluating vision encoders requires metrics that reliably predict their downstream performance in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Although recent studies have shown that cross-modal metrics can better capture such performance, unimodal metrics remain the dominant choice in practice. In this work, we revisit cross-modal evaluation of vision encoders through large-scale experiments. We identify important limitations in both the experimental design and methodological formulation of prior approaches. After addressing these limitations and introducing simple improvements, we propose RAVEL, a training-free method based on cross-modal nearest-neighbor retrieval. Despite its simplicity, RAVEL achieves state-of-the-art performance across our experiments, outperforming prior methods by a substantial margin. Our results demonstrate that simple cross-modal metrics, when evaluated under a careful and comprehensive setup, can provide a strong basis for evaluating vision encoders for MLLMs.
2610.05413.paper_summary_zh: 評估視覺編碼器需要能可靠預測其在多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs）中的下游表現的指標。儘管最近的研究顯示跨模態指標能更好地捕捉這種表現，但單模態指標在實踐中仍然是主流選擇。在本研究中，我們通過大規模實驗重新檢視視覺編碼器的跨模態評估。我們識別出先前方法在實驗設計和方法論制定上的重要限制。在解決這些限制並引入簡單改進後，我們提出了RAVEL，一種基於跨模態最近鄰檢索的無需訓練的方法。儘管其簡單，RAVEL在我們的實驗中達到了最先進的表現，顯著超越了先前的方法。我們的結果顯示，當在仔細且全面的設置下評估時，簡單的跨模態指標可以為評估MLLMs的視覺編碼器提供堅實的基礎。
